Do not sell red houses ($75 each) — only income and only monopoly. p2 on States has ~28% to hit a 1-house red ($90–$100) before my next roll; selling now kills that. Max liquidity $226, so Baltic hotel ($450) and 2-house greens bankrupt me anyway; pink 2-house rents are barely payable later. message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a Monopoly action.

Cash is $1 after paying $250 rent. Two properties are mortgaged. Kentucky Avenue has one house.

Indiana and Illinois each have one house. This red monopoly is the only income source. Opponent p3 has brown hotels and $447 cash. Opponent p2 has full pinks with two houses each. Opponent p4 has greens with two houses and utilities.

I cannot unmortgage or build. I am weighing whether to sell my three red houses for $225 or end the turn. Selling would leave me with $226 but remove my rent income.

The red houses generate $90, $90, and $100 in rent. Selling them for $75 each would be a major loss. I have no immediate debt to avoid bankruptcy. I will end the turn.

I will not sell the red houses preemptively. I will wait for a red rent to land before selling. I considered trading my mortgaged properties as blockers, but p2 has full pinks and previous negotiations failed.

P3 cannot complete any set with just one of my mortgaged properties. Vermont would still need Connecticut from p4, and New York would still need Tennessee from the bank. P2 does not need Vermont for a set either.

P4 has only $48, so any cash from selling a mortgaged property would be minimal. Building houses is impossible with just one dollar, and the cash would not fund safe construction anyway. The immediate danger is bankruptcy on the next bad landing.

Baltic Avenue is the next space after Mediterranean. It carries a $450 hotel rent. Any roll that lands me there would force house sales. I am weighing whether to sell now or wait for a red rent to land before I am forced to sell. The turn order is p2, then p3, then p4, then me.

P2 can reach my reds on the next roll. From States Avenue, rolling 8 lands on Kentucky, 10 on Indiana, and 11 on Illinois. P3 is past the reds and cannot hit them this lap.

P3 cannot reach my reds in one roll. The distance from Atlantic Avenue to Kentucky Avenue is 35 spaces, which is impossible. P4 is on the Community Chest at position 2, just after passing GO.

P4 cannot reach the reds in one roll. Only p2 has a chance to land on my reds next turn, with roughly a 28% probability of hitting Illinois, Indiana, or Kentucky. Collecting that rent would be life-saving.

I will keep the red houses and wait for p2 to land on them. Trading a mortgaged property would give p3 a path to orange or light blue, which is dangerous. I can only propose one trade per action.

The maximum cash I can raise by selling all three red houses is $226. That is still below the $450 hotel rent on Baltic Avenue. If p2 rolls a 1 and lands there, I would go bankrupt. The green properties owned by p4 also carry high two-house rents.

P4's greens at two houses would bankrupt me. Pacific, NC, and Penn each charge $390 to $450. P2's pinks at two houses would cost $200 to $220. Selling all three red houses for $226 leaves only $26 after paying $200 in rent. P3's other properties carry very low base rent.

I am now mapping the exact board positions. I am on Mediterranean at position 1. A roll of 1 lands on Baltic Avenue, which carries a $450 hotel rent and would force bankruptcy. I am checking whether other spaces like Community Chest or Park Place pose similar immediate threats.

I mapped the exact board positions. Rolling 1 lands on Community Chest at position 2. Rolling 2 lands on Baltic Avenue at position 3 with a $450 hotel rent that would bankrupt me. Rolling 3 lands on Income Tax at position 4 for $200, which I can cover by selling all three red houses and still have $26 left. Rolling 4 lands on Reading Railroad at position 5, costing $25, so I would need to sell one house. Rolling 5 lands on Oriental Avenue at position 6, owned by p3 without a monopoly, charging $6; I would sell one house to pay it and keep $70. Rolling 6 lands on Chance at position 7.

Rolls 8 through 12 are now mapped. Roll 8 lands on p4's mortgaged Connecticut, so no rent is collected. Roll 9 is just visiting Jail. Rolls 10 and 12 land on p2's St Charles and States at two houses each, costing $200 each. Roll 11 lands on p4's Electric Company; with one utility mortgaged, the multiplier drops to 4× dice, yielding about $44. All of these spaces are payable by selling one house.

The only immediate bankruptcy risk from my current position is rolling double ones to land on Baltic Avenue. That happens with probability 1/36, or roughly 2.8%. The other dangerous spaces are too far away for a single roll.

A chance card could land me on Boardwalk, but that space is mortgaged and would not charge rent. The expected value of keeping the red houses is positive because p2 might pay $90 to $100 on a hit, and I would survive to collect more later. Selling now for $225 would destroy the only income source while opponents still hold two-house sets and hotels.

I considered trading Vermont Avenue for cash from p2. They only have $151, so they cannot pay the previous $250 floor. That property would not help them complete a set, and they need their cash for pinks and greens. I am now checking whether p3 might pay for Vermont or New York.

P3 would not pay enough for Vermont to be worthwhile, and giving it away would let them later complete a light-blue set. P4 has only $48 and cannot afford anything useful. Proposing a trade would waste time without winning the game.

Cash is $1 after paying $250 rent. Two properties are mortgaged. Kentucky Avenue has one house.

Indiana and Illinois each have one house. This red monopoly is the only income source. Opponent p3 has brown hotels and $447 cash. Opponent p2 has full pinks with two houses each. Opponent p4 has greens with two houses and utilities.

I cannot unmortgage or build. I am weighing whether to sell my three red houses for $225 or end the turn. Selling would leave me with $226 but remove my rent income.

The red houses generate $90, $90, and $100 in rent. Selling them for $75 each would be a major loss. I have no immediate debt to avoid bankruptcy. I will end the turn.

I will not sell the red houses preemptively. I will wait for a red rent to land before selling. I considered trading my mortgaged properties as blockers, but p2 has full pinks and previous negotiations failed.

P3 cannot complete any set with just one of my mortgaged properties. Vermont would still need Connecticut from p4, and New York would still need Tennessee from the bank. P2 does not need Vermont for a set either.

P4 has only $48, so any cash from selling a mortgaged property would be minimal. Building houses is impossible with just one dollar, and the cash would not fund safe construction anyway. The immediate danger is bankruptcy on the next bad landing.

Baltic Avenue is the next space after Mediterranean. It carries a $450 hotel rent. Any roll that lands me there would force house sales. I am weighing whether to sell now or wait for a red rent to land before I am forced to sell. The turn order is p2, then p3, then p4, then me.

P2 can reach my reds on the next roll. From States Avenue, rolling 8 lands on Kentucky, 10 on Indiana, and 11 on Illinois. P3 is past the reds and cannot hit them this lap.

P3 cannot reach my reds in one roll. The distance from Atlantic Avenue to Kentucky Avenue is 35 spaces, which is impossible. P4 is on the Community Chest at position 2, just after passing GO.

P4 cannot reach the reds in one roll. Only p2 has a chance to land on my reds next turn, with roughly a 28% probability of hitting Illinois, Indiana, or Kentucky. Collecting that rent would be life-saving.

I will keep the red houses and wait for p2 to land on them. Trading a mortgaged property would give p3 a path to orange or light blue, which is dangerous. I can only propose one trade per action.

The maximum cash I can raise by selling all three red houses is $226. That is still below the $450 hotel rent on Baltic Avenue. If p2 rolls a 1 and lands there, I would go bankrupt. The green properties owned by p4 also carry high two-house rents.

P4's greens at two houses would bankrupt me. Pacific, NC, and Penn each charge $390 to $450. P2's pinks at two houses would cost $200 to $220. Selling all three red houses for $226 leaves only $26 after paying $200 in rent. P3's other properties carry very low base rent.

I am now mapping the exact board positions. I am on Mediterranean at position 1. A roll of 1 lands on Baltic Avenue, which carries a $450 hotel rent and would force bankruptcy. I am checking whether other spaces like Community Chest or Park Place pose similar immediate threats.

I mapped the exact board positions. Rolling 1 lands on Community Chest at position 2. Rolling 2 lands on Baltic Avenue at position 3 with a $450 hotel rent that would bankrupt me. Rolling 3 lands on Income Tax at position 4 for $200, which I can cover by selling all three red houses and still have $26 left. Rolling 4 lands on Reading Railroad at position 5, costing $25, so I would need to sell one house. Rolling 5 lands on Oriental Avenue at position 6, owned by p3 without a monopoly, charging $6; I would sell one house to pay it and keep $70. Rolling 6 lands on Chance at position 7.

Rolls 8 through 12 are now mapped. Roll 8 lands on p4's mortgaged Connecticut, so no rent is collected. Roll 9 is just visiting Jail. Rolls 10 and 12 land on p2's St Charles and States at two houses each, costing $200 each. Roll 11 lands on p4's Electric Company; with one utility mortgaged, the multiplier drops to 4× dice, yielding about $44. All of these spaces are payable by selling one house.

The only immediate bankruptcy risk from my current position is rolling double ones to land on Baltic Avenue. That happens with probability 1/36, or roughly 2.8%. The other dangerous spaces are too far away for a single roll.

A chance card could land me on Boardwalk, but that space is mortgaged and would not charge rent. The expected value of keeping the red houses is positive because p2 might pay $90 to $100 on a hit, and I would survive to collect more later. Selling now for $225 would destroy the only income source while opponents still hold two-house sets and hotels.

I considered trading Vermont Avenue for cash from p2. They only have $151, so they cannot pay the previous $250 floor. That property would not help them complete a set, and they need their cash for pinks and greens. I am now checking whether p3 might pay for Vermont or New York.

P3 would not pay enough for Vermont to be worthwhile, and giving it away would let them later complete a light-blue set. P4 has only $48 and cannot afford anything useful.
